# Development screen for claim-to-paper retrieval

Use SciFact's original training release and 5,183-document corpus. Split connected components of claims that share a cited source within training (regardless of stance) by deterministic SHA-256 of the sorted source IDs, using the first eight digest bytes modulo three. Two buckets fit hyperparameters; bucket zero screens the candidate. Include claims with at least one annotated evidence document. The official development release is reserved for a future locked comparison. Official test labels are private. Primary metric is query-average nDCG@10 using binary support or refutation evidence relevance.

Candidate extends BM25 plus BGE-small reciprocal-rank fusion with an evidence-sentence score. Match each query to an individual abstract sentence, highlighting a locally concentrated citation signal that whole-document averaging can dilute. Use maximum BM25 sentence score and combine its reciprocal rank with document BM25 and dense retrieval. Tune BM25 k1 in {.6,1.2,1.8} and b in {.25,.75}; tune sentence weight in {.25,.5,1,2}, dense weight in {.5,1,2}, and RRF constant in {10,60} on fitting queries only. Include document BM25, sentence BM25, author-style title/abstract TF-IDF, BGE-small standalone, tuned BM25–BGE hybrid, and lexical document–sentence fusion. Use all corpus documents for every policy and stable ID tie-breaking. Only advance if the candidate gains .02 nDCG over each control on screen with positive paired component-bootstrap lower endpoints (familywise 95%). Report all tested contrasts and leave the official evaluation untouched when a comparator fails. No end-to-end factual correctness or heritage-archive claim follows. The original P09 grounded-answer F1 margin applies to a separate endpoint.
